## Overview

Alim Khalelov is an AI-Native Product Manager with over 5 years of experience leading 0-to-1 product discovery and execution across AI software, monetization systems, and Web3 startups. Rather than stopping at static PRDs, he prototypes working interfaces directly in code, validates LLM outputs with deterministic evaluation checks, and builds fast-feedback distribution loops before scaling engineering investment. His recent track record includes growing a consumer launch from 0 to 10,000 users in 30 days, orchestrating automated publishing across 50+ content platforms, and winning both the GameDev AI Hackathon 2025 and the AI News Marketing Hackathon.

## Flagship Shipped Case Studies

### 1. Ocus: EU Crypto Compliance and Operations Cockpit
- Case Study URL: https://alim.dest.page/projects/ocus
- Live Demo: https://ocus-eu.vercel.app
- Documentation: https://alim.dest.page/wiki/ocus

Ocus is an institutional operations cockpit built for European digital asset teams navigating MiCA, DORA, and DAC8 regulatory mandates. The platform converts dense multi-agency legal text into an interactive 31-node Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with real-time critical path highlighting, dependency blocking indicators, a 15-week launch Gantt timeline, and Tier-1 banking integration readiness tracking. By separating regulatory dependencies into visual state layers, compliance leads immediately spot which legal bottleneck blocks go-live instead of drowning in static spreadsheets.

---

### 2. Nebuly: Weekly AI Brief and Executive Telemetry Platform
- Case Study URL: https://alim.dest.page/projects/nebuly
- Live Demo: https://alimkhalelov.github.io/nebuly/
- Documentation: https://alim.dest.page/wiki/nebuly

Nebuly is an executive intelligence prototype connecting high-level enterprise AI adoption narratives with conversation telemetry. Decision-makers often struggle to turn raw LLM interaction logs into tactical roadmap choices. Nebuly resolves this gap with interactive OHLC conversation trend views, three-order consequence simulations for product changes, and guardrailed enablement kits for cross-functional product teams. Every high-level insight drills straight back to verifiable session metrics without overwhelming non-technical stakeholders.

---

### 3. Plain: Minimalist Goal Clarification Workspace
- Case Study URL: https://alim.dest.page/projects/goal-classifier
- Live Demo: https://alimkhalelov.github.io/goal-classifier/
- Documentation: https://alim.dest.page/wiki/goal-classifier

Plain is a zero-build, minimalist strategic planner that diagnoses personal objectives across four concrete dimensions: Goal Statement, Time Horizon, Execution Plan, and Habit Regularity. It provides real-time heuristic classification (Fantasy, Task, Strategy, Success) alongside Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) AI strategic decomposition encrypted locally in the browser using the Web Crypto API (AES-GCM) so sensitive user plans never require server-side key custody.

---

### 4. Residual Intellect: AI Tech Radar and Automated Publishing Engine
- Case Study URL: https://alim.dest.page/projects/residual-intellect
- Live Demo: https://alimkhalelov.github.io/residual-intellect/
- Documentation: https://alim.dest.page/wiki/residual-intellect

Residual Intellect combines an interactive editorial promo site with a daily automated AI intelligence pipeline. It evaluates classic speculative fiction benchmarks from Gibson, Dick, Huxley, Orwell, and Pelevin against modern AI and hardware releases (measuring a 52-year average prophecy lag across 16+ archived forecasts), includes an interactive desktop-style quiz, and automates daily curated dispatches to Telegram (`@residual_intellect`).

---

### 5. Tempo: Progressive Interval and Kinematics Visualizer
- Case Study URL: https://alim.dest.page/projects/tempo
- Live Demo: https://alimkhalelov.github.io/tempo/
- Documentation: https://alim.dest.page/wiki/tempo

Tempo is a browser-native training HUD for runners and endurance athletes that replaces flat countdown timers with symmetric Push-Pull harmonic stages (`9 -> 6 -> 5 -> 3 -> 2 -> 3 -> 5 -> 6 -> 9`), dual-axis visual zooming (`up to 4.8x`), and a 60 FPS procedural SVG inverse kinematics runner. Focusing user attention strictly on the immediate sub-interval measurably lowers perceived cognitive drag during long endurance sets.
